style_when: the story is regulatory or contractual — a filing, a mandate, a rate notice, a certificate, a purchase order that changed the economics
prompt: Overhead flat-lay photograph, top-down 90-degree view, extreme asymmetric composition. A massive, thick stack of heavy, textured manila timecards sits dominantly on the left, dwarfing a single, thin, semi-translucent paper receipt resting on the right. Muted paper tones, visible tactile paper fibers, resting on a weathered oak desk surface. Even diffused daylight, soft directional cast shadows, no text or legible typography, one timecard slightly out of alignment to look handled. 50mm prime lens, razor-sharp edge-to-edge focus, premium editorial cover standard.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, watermarks, typography, logos, UI, unreadable text, human hands, people
rationale: The story is fundamentally about reading wage tables and uncovering the hidden administrative 'bill' of certification. A document flatlay elegantly contrasts the massive physical weight of time against the flimsy reality of the cash fee.
subject: a massive stack of timecards dwarfing a single thin receipt
core_thesis: The true cost of a certificate is the massive time investment required, not the minimal upfront exam fee.
core_conflict: Trivial upfront cash fee vs. massive hidden time investment.
